about:
# BagSmith

[![CurseForge](https://img.shields.io/badge/CurseForge-Download-F16436?style=for-the-badge&logo=curseforge&logoColor=white)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/bagsmith) [![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy_Me_a_Coffee-FFDD00?style=for-the-badge&logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/shweepy) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join_the_Community-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/uYfcHPkcar)

Spreadsheet-style bags for WoW Forever.

BagSmith replaces the game's bags with one window you can arrange your way: everything in a list or a grid of
icons, sorted into sections, searchable, with your bank and your other characters' bags a click away.

**Get it on [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/bagsmith).** This repository is BagSmith's source,
its plugin documentation and its tests. The main branch holds the latest development build; finished versions
are on CurseForge and under this repository's Releases.

## Features

- **List or Icons view**, in a Classic look that matches the game or a flat Modern one.
- **Sections:** items grouped by type, by bag, or all together; sections of your own that you fill by hand or
  with rules, pinned sections, and an optional split of Consumables into Food, Drink, Potions and more.
- **Sorting, Merge Stacks and search,** with filters and saved views as tabs (sheets).
- **Your bank and other characters,** including their bags, gold and currencies.
- **Item icons that tell you more:** item level, junk, gear sets, Pawn upgrades and cooldowns, with Icon Corners
  to choose what shows where, and marks from other addons too.
- **Helpers:** marking and selling junk, a Disenchant Helper for enchanters with Results for what your disenchants
  gave you, and optional auto-confirm for some yes/no boxes, all off until you turn them on.
- **Works with other addons, none required:** auction prices from Auctionator or Blackthornes Tradeskills, and
  what ItemTree and Pawn know about your items.
- **Plugins:** a public API for other addons, and a gamepad companion, BagSmith Gamepad (in alpha).

## Installing

From CurseForge, or download a release here and put the `BagSmith` folder in your game's `Interface/AddOns`
folder (the `BagSmith_Gamepad` folder too, if you want the companion). Then `/bs settings` opens Settings, and
`/bs new` shows what's new.

## For addon authors

Start with [docs/README.md](https://github.com/Shweep8/bagsmith/blob/main/docs/README.md): adding marks to BagSmith's item icons, writing a plugin, the full API,
and a starter plugin in [BagSmith_ExamplePlugin](https://github.com/Shweep8/bagsmith/blob/main/BagSmith_ExamplePlugin). The docs and the example plugin are
MIT licensed.

## Running the tests

BagSmith's tests run outside the game against a mock WoW client. You need Python 3 and the `lupa` package:

    pip install lupa
    python3 tools/run_tests.py                     # everything (a few minutes; several sets at once)
    python3 tools/run_tests.py some_set_tests.lua  # one or more sets, by file name or path

Run them from the repository root (the folder holding `BagSmith/`). `tests/README.md` explains how the sets are
organized. Mock results show the code's behaviour, not the real game client's.

## Contributing

Pull requests are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Shweep8/bagsmith/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) first: ask before changing how BagSmith
behaves for everyone, keep each pull request to one change, and run the tests.

## Support and feedback

- Bugs and requests: open an issue here, or comment on CurseForge.
- Chat: the [BagSmith Discord](https://discord.gg/uYfcHPkcar).
- If BagSmith saves you time: [Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/shweepy).

## License

BagSmith is copyright (c) 2026 Shweep, all rights reserved. The plugin docs and the example plugin are MIT
licensed, and the bundled libraries and two toolbar icons keep their own licenses. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/Shweep8/bagsmith/blob/main/LICENSE).

releases.name: BagSmith 1.11.0
releases.notes:
## BagSmith 1.11.0

### New

Gear sets can be made from your bags any time. The Gear Sets tab keeps a New Gear Set button under your sets and shows how many of the game's limit you have, and each set's menu has Rename..., Delete... and New Gear Set... Before, the button went away after your first set.

New Section From This Item offers more to tick when it's true of the item: its kind of consumable (Food, Drink, Potions and so on), Quest Item, Crafting Material, whether you can use it (for gear and recipes), and, with ItemTree, what it knows about the item.

Auto-Open and Auto-Close (Settings > Automations): a switch for each place your bags open by themselves (vendors, the mailbox, trades, the auction house, the bank and the guild bank), and a When I Leave choice: Always Close, Close If Auto-Opened or Never Close. Every switch starts ticked, and When I Leave starts on Always Close.

Sections on a Sheet (Settings > Custom Sections, or a section's menu in your bags): pick a sheet and tick the sections of yours that should show there only, several at once.

Disenchant Results: the Disenchant Helper has a Results button. It shows what your disenchants gave you, This Session and All Time: how many items by quality, the materials with their auction house value now, what the items would have sold for instead, and the most valuable item you disenchanted. The sold-instead lines count disenchants from this version on, compare only the ones whose materials BagSmith saw, take the auction house's 5% cut off both sides, and name no winner when an item had no auction price at the time. The Helper's own count now says how many you disenchanted just now and how many this session.

See what the Disenchant Helper holds back: a Held Back line at the end of its list shows those items when you click it, each with a lock, its reason and its vendor, auction and materials values. Disenchant Anyway puts one piece in the list when you would rather decide for yourself (asked first for a favorite, a gear set piece, an epic, your Exclusion List, and refundable or tradeable items), and Hold Back takes it out again. An offer is for that one piece and ends when you close the Helper.

### Changed

Auto-Close Bags I Opened, from 1.10.1, is now the When I Leave choice on Automations. What you had carries over: ticked is Always Close, unticked is Close If Auto-Opened.

Always Close now also closes bags you already had open when you finish a trade or leave the guild bank, as it always has at vendors, the mailbox, the bank and the auction house.

Special Bag Slot Indicators (Settings > Item Icons): pick a kind of bag from a list and set up its indicator, instead of scrolling a column of twelve switches.

Settings shows BagSmith's version number beside its title.

A menu too long for your screen shows arrows at its top and bottom, so you can see there is more and click to reach it. The mouse wheel still scrolls it.

The lists for a Type, Slot or Section rule open in a taller window when your screen has room, so more of a long list shows at once.

### Fixed

Leaving the mailbox closed bags you had opened yourself even with Auto-Close Bags I Opened turned off (1.10.1). When I Leave now holds at the mailbox as it does at a vendor.

releases.name: BagSmith 1.10.1
releases.notes:
## BagSmith 1.10.1

### New

Auto-Close Bags I Opened (Settings > General), on as it has always worked. Turn it off and bags you opened yourself stay open when you leave a vendor, the mailbox, a trade or the auction house. Bags that opened by themselves still close.

### Fixed

Bags that stayed shut at vendors, the mailbox, trades and the auction house. With the game's Use Combined Bags turned off, the game's own bag call could close BagSmith the instant it opened, so nothing showed up. Opening with your bag key always worked.

### Changed

Settings > General: Open with the Bag Keybind names the key your bags are really on, such as Tab, instead of always saying B.

releases.name: BagSmith 1.10.0
releases.notes:
## BagSmith 1.10.0

### New

Custom sections can fill themselves. Alt+Left-click an item and pick New Section From This Item, tick what the items should have in common with it (its type, slot, quality or binding), and see what would go in the section before you create it.

When an item fits more than one of your sections, the higher one in Settings > Custom Sections gets it. Arrows there change their order, and each section shows its rules in words.

A rule editor for your sections. Click the pencil beside a section in Settings > Custom Sections, or pick Edit Section... from the section's menu, to give it rules about an item's type, slot, quality, binding, item level or vendor value. Choose whether an item has to fit all of them or any one, and see what would go in the section, and what fits but stays somewhere else, before you save. New Section... on that page opens it too.

The Filters window is rebuilt around the same rules. Quality and quick picks (New, Usable by Me) sit at the top. Under "Only show items that fit" you add rules with + Add a Rule, choose all of these or any one of these, and see how many items are left. Three rules are just for filters: Section, Bag and Time in Bags.

Save as Section... in the Filters window opens the section editor with the rules you've set, so a filter you like can become a section.

A section can show on every sheet, or only on some. In the section editor, set Show this section on to only some sheets and tick the tabs. Everywhere else its items stay in their usual section, so Cloth, Leather and Herbs can split up your Trade Goods tab while All keeps one Trade Goods section.

With the ItemTree addon installed, your section and filter rules can use what it knows: Used by My Professions, Needed for a Quest, An Upgrade for Me and Sold by Vendors, and for filters ItemTree's Advice. Settings > Addon Sources turns it on or off. ItemTree is optional, and BagSmith works the same without it.

With ItemTree, the Loot Helper and Disenchant Helper also hold back an item ItemTree says to keep. They show it with the other items they don't offer, and each Helper has its own switch in Settings > Addon Sources. A piece ItemTree keeps for its dust still shows in the Disenchant Helper, and the Loot Helper still offers your junk. While its switch is on and ItemTree hasn't answered about an item yet, that item is held back under Waiting for ItemTree. The Helper checks again by itself, and offers the item only if ItemTree doesn't say to keep it. Clear Soul Shards is your own action with its own count to keep, and doesn't ask ItemTree.

With Pawn, the Disenchant Helper can hold back a piece Pawn says is an upgrade for you. That switch is in Settings > Addon Sources too, and it's off until you turn it on.

A new Settings page, Addon Sources, shows what BagSmith does with Auctionator, Blackthornes Tradeskills, ItemTree and Pawn, each in its own card with a switch for each job.

More rules for your sections and filters: Name (its name contains a word you type), Food, Drink and Potions (what kind of consumable it is), Quest Item, Crafting Material and Usable by Me. + Add a Rule lists the rules in groups.

Settings > Custom Sections can start a section from an example (Cloth, Herbs, Gear to Sell, Food and Drink): it opens filled in for you to look over. The page also shows the order an item finds its section in.

All Items is part of Section Order. With Sections: All, a pinned, Favorites or other dynamic section shows above All Items when it comes before it in Section Order, and below when it comes after. Drag the All Items title, or use the arrows in Settings > Sections, to choose.

### Changed

The Gear, Consumables, Trade Goods, Quest and Junk tabs show every item of their kind, grouped under your own sections where you have them. Before, an item in one of your sections left its tab.

The boxes the Filters window used to have (Type / Sections, Bind, Where and Age) are rules now. Sheets you saved before show them as rules and filter the same.

An item you move back to its usual section by hand stays there, even when one of your sections would take it.

The Disenchant Helper no longer offers an item you've marked as junk. Mark one there and it leaves the list, and it comes back if you take the mark off.

Price Source moved from Settings > General to the new Addon Sources page, and is now called Auction Price Source.

The Loot Helper holding back Pawn upgrades is a switch now, in Settings > Addon Sources. It's on, as before.

Pin to Top is now Pin Section, and Unpin is Unpin Section. A pinned section still goes ahead of your other sections; with Sections: All it can now sit below All Items if you put it there.

With Sections: All, Favorites no longer drops below All Items when a Keys section is showing, and Gear Sets no longer jumps above it when you have favorites. Each follows Section Order.

Settings: Plugins moved down the list, just above Advanced.

The rule editor no longer cuts a long rule name short, such as Used by My Professions.

Classic skin: item icons and their borders are cleaner in Icons and List view, with the artwork kept inside the border. Bold now brightens Classic borders. Thanks to Jeor!

releases.name: BagSmith 1.9.8
releases.notes:
## BagSmith 1.9.8

### Fixed

Characters who share a first name on the same ruleset no longer write over each other. They were saved as one character, so each saw only itself in Global Inventory and item tooltips, and could show the other's bank as its own. Each now has its own saved record. If you have characters like that, log in to each and visit the bank once, so its bank is saved fresh.

A character can no longer be taken for a new one when the game is slow to report its level at login, which would have hidden its other characters. One that was finds its saved data again the next time it logs in.

What's New: the row of update buttons wraps onto a second line instead of running off the window.

### Changed

What's New opens by itself once for this update, which patches don't usually do, so the note above about characters who share a first name reaches you sooner.

What's New: closing the window clears the NEW tags on its updates, so NEW means "since you last looked".

releases.name: BagSmith 1.9.7
releases.notes:
BagSmith 1.9.7

Fixed
Dim Junk: junk keeps its greyed look while your bags are being cleaned up. Before, it flashed back to full color until the Clean Up finished, most of all with Clean Up Bags When Opened on.

Changed
Clean Up Bags When Opened no longer runs when your bags open at a vendor, so your items stay put while you sell. Sell Junk Automatically also no longer misses junk that the Clean Up was moving at that moment. The Clean Up button still works there.
